findings.summary: `rules += active_promos(now)` mutates the cached list returned by load_rules in place, so promos are re-applied on every quote (discounts compound), expired promos persist, and /rules in api.py returns promos as tenant rules.
The cache returns a shared mutable list, so any caller that sorts or appends to it changes what all later callers see.
The per-process cache has no expiry, so a rule change saved in one worker leaves other workers serving stale rules until restart.
cache_clear() drops every tenant's cache entry on each save instead of only the changed tenant's.
The second test changes global DB state without cleaning up, and no test calls price_quote twice, so the cache mutation bug would go undetected.
